title: Dynamics of Erased Distinctions
summary: A living synthesis of the project’s current view of coarse-graining: closure tracks which distinctions remain causally relevant, how erased distinctions return to visibility, and when representation repair must restore them.
thesis: Groovy Commutator studies the dynamics of distinctions erased by a representation.

title: Dimensional Closure and the Commutator Lift
summary: Transverse intervention independence now supplies an operational axis witness beyond state capacity: separated Rule90 channels have unbounded constant-support native intervention rank, while copied width does not; even with unlimited total 1D storage, a fixed alphabet and fixed common local endpoint window eventually cannot preserve all channel actions. This remains a representation-relative resource theorem, not an intrinsic-dimension criterion.
thesis: When two dynamical paths fail to commute, represent the disagreement as a new coordinate and ask whether the enlarged representation closes.

title: Invariants Across Representation Contracts
summary: Eleven audits complete across four transformation types: global relabelings, an injective local recoding, linear and non-linear observations, and a change of wiring. Reflection and coprime whole-contract dilation preserve every exact property audited, with the seeded sweep labels only stable; complement conjugation and dilation are exactly covariant only when the companion object, the derivative or the observation, is transported with the rule; closure under an observation and its history cost are properties of the pair and are genuinely changed. A twelfth audit, factor locality on observation images, is accepted: idempotent observations bound the factor radius by construction, and the one whole-ring factor coincides with the one ring-dependent closure. The Program page carries the verdict matrix and what each other program can use.
thesis: Which properties of a represented dynamics survive a declared change of representation contract, after transporting what must be transported, and at what cost?
